title: Dual-Sim / Sim-Video-Guided World Model
description: Survey a dual-simulation architecture in which a physics-based simulator supplies cross-embodiment kinematics, motion video and proprioception, while a diffusion/transformer world-model simulator preserves real-scene appearance and predicts future video plus robot state.
summary: Dual-Sim couples two simulators rather than asking one video model to learn every embodiment mapping. The physics simulator converts task and action into kinematic trajectory, standardized robot-motion video and proprioception; the world-model simulator combines them with the real initial image/state to predict photorealistic future video and robot state. The overview, sim-context adapter and A/B1/B2 figures are design proposals, not validated results.
asset_alt: Dual-Sim overview separating a physics-based simulator for cross-embodiment kinematics, robot-motion video, and proprioception from a world-model simulator for photorealistic future video and robot state.
asset_caption: 总览：Physics Simulator 将任务与动作变成运动学轨迹、统一机器人运动视频和本体状态；World-Model Simulator 再结合初始图像与状态生成真实感未来视频和未来机器人状态。跨本体泛化与 VLA 闭环核验仍是待验证假设。

details.text: Core dual-simulation split: the physics-based simulator owns embodiment-specific kinematics and dynamics, and emits a kinematic trajectory, standardized robot-motion video, and proprioception state. The world-model simulator combines those conditions with the real initial image/state to generate photorealistic future video plus future robot state. This is the proposed cross-embodiment interface; it still needs matched embodiment, state-accuracy and closed-loop VLA validation.

Trainable sim-context adapter: encode simulator video with a frozen VAE, then pass sim tokens through a context tower that reuses frozen GE-Sim block weights with sim-only LoRA. Full-zero projections inject pixel-aligned residuals into the frozen GE-Sim V2 Video DiT at depths 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22 and 26, while the original 27-channel input path and pretrained backbone stay frozen. Validate alignment, adapter capacity and sim-appearance leakage before treating this as a working route.

Trainable route: encode multi-view initial frames, future actions, optional robot state and embodiment/URDF together with a fixed multi-view sim-video condition. Background tokens may attend only to real-image context; robot tokens may additionally attend to sim-video; sim tokens neither read from nor get updated by generated tokens. The intended separation is simulator-owned motion and embodiment versus foundation-model-owned appearance.

Training-free route B1: freeze GE-Sim V2, extract motion with temporal differences plus spatial low-pass filtering, compare predicted and simulator motion representations, and backpropagate the resulting energy only through the sampling latent. It avoids a robot mask, but assumes the motion representation suppresses appearance strongly enough.

Training-free route B2: freeze the base world model and minimize latent distance to the sim-video only inside a robot-region mask. A timestep-adaptive schedule warms up the constraint, keeps it strong through the structure-and-motion phase, then decays it so the base model can recover realistic materials, lighting and contact details.

The first useful comparison is route A versus B1 versus B2 on identical initial frames, actions and simulator rollouts. Report motion/pose fidelity, background leakage, appearance preservation, contact and object-state consistency, temporal flicker, runtime, peak memory and robustness to camera, embodiment and sim-to-real mismatch.

risks_decisions: Keep this as a standalone Survey card. Self-Improving Agents owns environment-generation Harness and regression-gated workflow evolution; Dual-Sim owns the narrower hypothesis that simulator motion priors can guide realistic robot-video prediction.

The overview, sim-context adapter and three route figures are architecture proposals only. Do not claim training success, better video quality, motion fidelity or sim-to-real benefit until matched baselines and ablations are reported.

The main technical risk is control leakage: too little guidance loses robot kinematics, while too much copies simulator appearance or damages contact and scene consistency. Measure both robot-region fidelity and non-robot-region preservation.
B1 and B2 are alternatives, not cumulative evidence. B1 depends on motion features being appearance-invariant; B2 depends on reliable robot masks and aligned simulator/real latent coordinates.
The public chengaopro/Dual-Sim repository name collides with this broader video-guidance concept. Keep task-porting evidence and method-validation evidence labeled separately.
